---
title: "Stage 1 — Q2 real data: the authors' GLMM"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
engine: knitr
---

**Goal.** Refit Q2's `mod2` (abundance at natural trees ~ TreePerimeter + Aspect + DistReef + (1 | LocationID), NB1) next to the same model without the location term, and ask one question: are the residuals spatially correlated? This is the baseline every later stage is compared against.

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("../sim/_load.R")
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(GGally)
library(ggspatial)
library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(patchwork)

HTrees2 <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "abundance.only.natural.trees.txt"),
                      header = TRUE, dec = ".")
```

## The data

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original code"}
[`script_question2_abundance.R`](../../R%20code/script_question2_abundance.R) lines 16–19 (`read.table`), 49–50 and 100–102 (`pairs()` collinearity plots; ggpairs here) and 52–61 (the collinearity comments).
:::
First, let's see what we are working with:
```{r}
head(HTrees2)
```
Making `SizeCat` and `Aspect` into factors will make downstream analysis cleaner, so let's do it here:
```{r}
HTrees2 = HTrees2 |>
  mutate(
    SizeCat = as.factor(SizeCat),
    Aspect = as.factor(Aspect)
  )
```

Now, let's do a basic smellcheck for collinearity (how much do each variable covary with each other?) - if we have highly collinear data, our model won't know which variable to attribute variation to, and we may run into issues with model fit among other issues.
```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=12, message=FALSE}
ggpairs(
  data = HTrees2 |> select(!c('LocationID','Label', 'Lat', 'Long')),
  upper = list(continuous = "cor", combo = "blank", discrete = "blank")
)
```

From the above, it seems that:

1) With respect to abundance, `TreePerimeter` has a large positive correlation (makes sense if we hypothesize they like structure, which we do) and `DistReef` has a strong negative correlation (also makes sense if we assume fish come from reef, so further away is worse).
2) `DistReef` and `DistIsland` are collinear and correlation is negative - makes sense as we expect if you're closer to the reef you are probably farther from the island since the reef is not on the island. Likely we don't want to include both in a model together. If we use a rule of thumb, many of these covariates probably shouldn't be included together (`DistIsland` and `Trees50` for eg, `DistReef` and `WMI` for eg). Per the authors' comments:

```
# From here you gather that the following variables cannot go as predictors
# in the same model because they are highly correlated to each other:
# Lat cant go with Long
# Lat cant go with DistIsland
# Lat shouldnt go with DistReef
# Long cant go with DistIsland
# Long cant go with Trees50
# DistIsland cant go with Trees50
# DistReef cant go in with Trees 50
# DistReef perhaps shouldn't go in with WMI (but correlation is low)
```

3) Fortunately for us, `DistReef` and `TreePerimeter` are not collinear (ie, they are largely independent) which is great.

## The models

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original code"}
[`script_question2_abundance.R`](../../R%20code/script_question2_abundance.R) lines 232–236, `mod2 <- glmmTMB(...)` and `summary(mod2)`. `mod0` has no counterpart; the authors' alternative is the Poisson GLM `mod1`, lines 157–162.
:::
Now fitting the model:
```{r}
mod2 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ TreePerimeter + Aspect + DistReef
                   + (1 | LocationID),
                family = nbinom1(),
                data = HTrees2)
summary(mod2)
```
Authors do a bit more model selection, but their choice of model looks good. We have a nbinom1 (which scales variance linearly with the mean given the input covariates). The dispersion parameter is larger than 1 (which would imply Poisson by itself would be fine), so nbinom1 is probably(?) a good choice.

To have something to compare against, let's also fit the exact same model *without* the location random intercept. The authors' own counter model (`mod1`) swaps the family, adds covariates and an interaction all at once, so it's hard to say what any difference is due to. Here, the only thing that changes is the `(1 | LocationID)` term:
```{r}
mod0 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ TreePerimeter + Aspect + DistReef,
                family = nbinom1(),
                data = HTrees2)
summary(mod0)
```
For the record - `(1 | LocationID)` is not really "spatial". It says the two rows (e and s) at the same tree share something, but nothing about neighboring trees being similar. The actually spatial models come later (stage 4).

From here on every diagnostic is shown for both models side by side. Each model flavor gets its own colour (`model_palette` in `sim/model_compare.R`) which stays fixed for the GAMs and spatial basis models later on:
```{r}
cmp <- compare_models(list("No location" = mod0, "Location RE" = mod2), HTrees2)
```

## Residuals

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original code"}
[`script_question2_abundance.R`](../../R%20code/script_question2_abundance.R) lines 241–250 (Pearson residuals vs fitted values for `mod2`), and residuals vs each covariate: 261–267 (`TreePerimeter`), 270–275 (`Aspect`), 278–284 (`DistIsland`), 287–293 (`DistReef`) and 296–302 (`WMI`).
:::
Let's look at the linear part of the model and it's associated residuals first:

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
# model checks and validation:
ggplot(cmp$obs, aes(x = fitted, y = pearson, colour = flavor)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ flavor) +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  ylab("Pearson residuals") +
  xlab("Fitted values")
```

The authors check Pearson residuals against every covariate (`TreePerimeter`, `Aspect`, `DistIsland`, `DistReef`, `WMI`) and call them all "ok". If the residuals are independent of the inputs, they should show no trend against any of them, whether or not the covariate is in the model (`DistIsland` and `WMI` aren't). Here are the four continuous ones, with a loess smooth and the correlation between residual and covariate in each panel (`Aspect` gets its own boxplot in the next section). `DistReef` is the one that is basically a spatial coordinate - if there's leftover spatial structure, this is one of the first places I'd expect it to show up once we start simulating:

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6, message=FALSE}
resid_cov <- cmp$obs |>
  select(flavor, pearson, TreePerimeter, DistIsland, DistReef, WMI) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(flavor, pearson), names_to = "covariate", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(covariate = factor(covariate, levels = c("TreePerimeter", "DistIsland", "DistReef", "WMI")))

# Pearson correlation between residual and covariate, with its p-value
resid_cor <- resid_cov |>
  group_by(flavor, covariate) |>
  summarise(r = cor(value, pearson), p = cor.test(value, pearson)$p.value, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(resid_cov, aes(x = value, y = pearson, colour = flavor)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_label(data = resid_cor, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = sprintf("r = %.2f, p = %.2f", r, p)),
             hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(flavor ~ covariate, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Covariate value", y = "Pearson residuals",
       caption = "Line: loess smooth. r: Pearson correlation between residual and covariate.")
```

## Are the residuals clumped within a tree?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original code"}
[`script_question2_abundance.R`](../../R%20code/script_question2_abundance.R) lines 270–275, `boxplot(E1 ~ Aspect)`: the same residual boxplot, grouped by `Aspect` rather than `LocationID`. The partner correlation has no counterpart.
:::
The models assume every count's residual is independent of every other's. Each tree here was counted twice (east and south), so the most basic way that can fail is for a tree's two residuals to move together: if something about a tree that the model doesn't know about raises or lowers both counts, both residuals land on the same side of zero. That's clumping *within* a site; the spatial checks further down ask about similarity *between* nearby sites.

First, the authors' residual boxplot (they plot `boxplot(E1 ~ Treatment)` and `boxplot(E1 ~ Aspect)`), here by `LocationID`: each box spans one tree's two Pearson residuals (points: e = east, s = south), with trees ordered from the lowest to the highest mean residual within each model:

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.2}
cmp$obs |>
  group_by(flavor, LocationID) |>
  mutate(site_mean = mean(pearson)) |>
  group_by(flavor) |>
  mutate(site_rank = dense_rank(site_mean)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = site_rank, y = pearson, colour = flavor)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group = site_rank), outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Aspect), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ flavor, ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(e = 16, s = 1), name = "Aspect") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  xlab("Trees (LocationID), ordered by mean residual") +
  ylab("Pearson residuals")
```

Then one number for the same idea, the **partner correlation**: the correlation between each tree's east residual and its south residual, across the 24 trees (left). To judge it, the same shuffle as the Moran's I test: pair each east residual with a randomly chosen tree's south residual instead, 999 times, so that partners are unrelated by construction (right; dashed line at 0, line = real):

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.9}
set.seed(215)
partner_cmp <- partner_check(list("No location" = mod0, "Location RE" = mod2), HTrees2, nsim = 999)

p_pairs <- ggplot(partner_cmp$pairs, aes(x = r_e, y = r_s, colour = flavor)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ flavor, ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "East residual", y = "South residual (same tree)")

p_perm <- ggplot(filter(partner_cmp$perm, !real), aes(x = r, fill = flavor)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(data = filter(partner_cmp$perm, real), aes(xintercept = r, colour = flavor), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_label(data = filter(partner_cmp$perm, real),
             aes(x = r, y = Inf, label = sprintf("real r = %.2f\np = %.3f", r, p)),
             vjust = 1.2, hjust = -0.05, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ flavor, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_model(guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Partner correlation (histogram = 999 shuffles, line = real)", y = "Shuffles")

p_pairs + p_perm + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.8))
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Interpretation:**
Without a site term, a tree's east and south residuals agree far more than random pairings ever do. The two counts per tree aren't independent, which is exactly the dependence the authors' (1 | LocationID) is there to account for in random effect model. More specifically the two residuals at a tree are positively correlated across trees (r = 0.59), far more than random pairings produce.
:::

## Are the residuals spatially correlated?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original code"}
[`script_question2_abundance.R`](../../R%20code/script_question2_abundance.R) lines 305–322: the random-intercept bubble map (`ranef(mod2)` on Lat/Long). The residual map, lineup and Moran's I have no counterpart.
:::
Next, the residuals on the map. Each point is one `LocationID`, showing the mean Pearson residual of its two rows. Filled = more fish than the model predicts, open = fewer, size = how much. This version works for any model (including the GAMs later, which won't have a random intercept to pull out):

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
ggplot(cmp$loc, aes(x = Long, y = Lat, colour = flavor,
                    size = abs(mean_pearson), shape = mean_pearson >= 0)) +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "osm", progress = "none",
                      cachedir = file.path(results_dir, "basemap")) +
  geom_point(stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ flavor) +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = "more than predicted", `FALSE` = "fewer than predicted"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6, name = "|mean Pearson residual|") +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326, default_crs = 4326,
           xlim = range(cmp$loc$Long) + c(-0.006, 0.006),   # ~600 m of context around the sites
           ylim = range(cmp$loc$Lat) + c(-0.006, 0.006)) +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "lines")) +
  labs(caption = "Map tiles © OpenStreetMap contributors")
```

And the authors' actual check for spatial autocorrelation - instead of looking at the residuals directly, they pull out the random intercept for each `LocationID` and plot it on the map. This one only exists for `mod2`. Red = location has fewer fish than the fixed effects predict, blue = more, size = how much:

```{r}
# Checking for spatial autocorrelation of residuals:
ai <- ranef(mod2)$cond$LocationID$`(Intercept)`
MyData = data.frame(ai = ai,
                    Lat = tapply(HTrees2$Lat, FUN = mean, INDEX = HTrees2$LocationID),
                    Lon = tapply(HTrees2$Long, FUN = mean, INDEX = HTrees2$LocationID))
plot(x = MyData$Lon,
     y = MyData$Lat,
     type = "n")
MyCol <- c("red","blue") [as.numeric(MyData$ai>= 0)+1]
MyCex <- 5 * abs(ai) / max(ai)
points(
  x = MyData$Lon,
  y = MyData$Lat,
  col = MyCol,
  cex = MyCex,
  pch = 1
)
# Random effects for Location, spatially un-correlated.
```

The authors' conclusion is "spatially un-correlated", i.e. no obvious clumps of red or blue. This is the plot we should return to when we crank up autocorrelation, artificially, when we simualte later on. At some point, this should start to look clumpy, because we do not provide the model any way to account for the fact that some sites are nearer to each other than other sites, only that there might be some residual shared within a site. 

That said, looking at the map above it does kind of look clumped to me (in that there are some negative residuals lumped together in the cetner of the map). But, let's see how weird that really is: the middle map below is the real set of random intercepts, and the other eight are the *same* 24 values shuffled randomly among the locations (i.e., bootstrapping what it looks like when there is no spatial pattern at all, by construction). If the real one doesn't stand out from its neighbors, the clumping isn't convincing:

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
set.seed(215)

lineup <- cmp$loc |>
  filter(flavor == "Location RE") |>
  select(LocationID, Long, Lat, ranef) |>
  list() |>
  rep(9) |>
  imap(\(d, i) if (i == 5) d else mutate(d, ranef = sample(ranef))) |>   # panel 5 (the middle) = real
  bind_rows(.id = "panel") |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = 1:9))

ggplot(lineup, aes(x = Long, y = Lat, size = abs(ranef), shape = ranef >= 0)) +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "osm", progress = "none",
                      cachedir = file.path(results_dir, "basemap")) +
  geom_point(colour = model_palette[["Location RE"]], stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 3,
             labeller = as_labeller(\(x) if_else(x == "5", "Real", "Shuffled"))) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = "more than predicted", `FALSE` = "fewer than predicted"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6, name = "|random intercept|") +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326, default_crs = 4326,
           xlim = range(lineup$Long) + c(-0.002, 0.002),
           ylim = range(lineup$Lat) + c(-0.002, 0.002)) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),   # coordinates don't matter for a lineup
        axis.title = element_blank()) +
  labs(caption = "Map tiles © OpenStreetMap contributors")
```

Eyeballing 9 maps is a start, but we can do the same thing 999 times and try to glean something more quantatitative. A really easy-to-understand approach is, if we take the correlation of the a given locations' residual against their nearest neighbors' residuals, we would expect that number to be positive IF we see spatial autocorrelation, and much closer to 0 if we don't see spatial autocorrelation. Essentially, when we randomly shuffle locations, we simulate a scenario where space has NO impact on the residual and compare our real observed aggregated residual. This is essentially 'Morans' I test' for spatial autocorrelation


```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
nb_weights <- cmp$loc |>
  filter(flavor == "Location RE") |>                     # one row per location (same for every flavor)
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Long", "Lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32760) |>                                 # UTM 60S, so distances are in meters
  knearneigh(k = 4) |>
  knn2nb() |>
  nb2listw(style = "W")

set.seed(215)
moran <- cmp$loc |>
  group_by(flavor) |>
  group_modify(\(d, k) {
    mc <- moran.mc(d$mean_pearson, nb_weights, nsim = 999)
    tibble(I = mc$res, real = seq_along(mc$res) == length(mc$res), p = mc$p.value)
  }) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(filter(moran, !real), aes(x = I, fill = flavor)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -1 / (length(nb_weights$neighbours) - 1), linetype = 2) +   # E[I] = -1/(n-1), n = 24 locations
  annotate("text", x = -1 / (length(nb_weights$neighbours) - 1), y = 0, label = "expected with\nno pattern",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  geom_vline(data = filter(moran, real), aes(xintercept = I, colour = flavor), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_label(data = filter(moran, real), aes(x = I, y = Inf, label = sprintf("real I = %.2f\np = %.3f", I, p)),
             vjust = 1.2, hjust = -0.05, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ flavor) +
  scale_fill_model(guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_model(guide = "none") +
  xlab("Moran's I of the location-mean Pearson residuals (histogram = 999 shuffles, line = real)") +
  ylab("Shuffles")
```

## What changes between the models

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original code"}
[`script_question2_abundance.R`](../../R%20code/script_question2_abundance.R) line 236, `summary(mod2)` (the fixed-effect table).
:::
The fixed effects from both models, estimate ± 95% CI:

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
ggplot(cmp$coef, aes(x = estimate, y = term, colour = flavor)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lwr, xmax = upr),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_colour_model(name = NULL) +
  xlab("Estimate (log scale)") +
  ylab(NULL)
```

`DistReef` is in meter, so its coefficient is per meters and looks tiny on this scale.

## Save for the simulations

Everything the simulations need goes into one file, as three tidy tables: the "truth" (`mod2`'s estimates, which become the parameters we simulate from), the design (one row per observation, without the response), and the locations (one row per tree, with coordinates in meters for the spatial stages):

```{r}
#| label: save
truth <- bind_rows(
  tibble(type = "beta",  parameter = names(fixef(mod2)$cond), value = unname(fixef(mod2)$cond)),
  tibble(type = "sigma", parameter = "LocationID", value = attr(VarCorr(mod2)$cond$LocationID, "stddev")[[1]]),
  tibble(type = "phi",   parameter = "nbinom1",    value = sigma(mod2))   # NB1: Var = mu * (1 + phi)
)

design <- HTrees2 |>
  select(LocationID, Aspect, TreePerimeter, DistReef, Lat, Long)

locations <- HTrees2 |>
  distinct(LocationID, Lat, Long) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Long", "Lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(32760) |>                                     # UTM 60S, meters
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
         y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  as_tibble()

saveRDS(list(truth = truth, design = design, locations = locations),
        file.path(results_dir, "stage1.rds"))
```

Reading it back, which is exactly what the later stages do:

```{r}
stage1 <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "stage1.rds"))
stage1$truth
glimpse(stage1$design)
glimpse(stage1$locations)
```
